title: How to Layer Indian Outfits in Winter Abroad: Coats, Shawls and Boots
excerpt: How to layer Indian outfits in winter abroad: coats, shawls, thermals and boots that keep kurta sets and Anarkalis warm in UK, Canada and US cold.
body:
You can wear your kurta sets and Anarkalis right through a UK, Canadian or US winter: wear thermals underneath, pick a coat long enough to cover the kurta hem, and finish with a shawl and ankle or knee boots. The secret is planning your layers around the silhouette, so you stay warm outdoors and still look festive once the coat comes off.

## Start with a hidden base layer

Warmth begins under the outfit, not on top of it.

- **Thermal leggings** in skin tone or black replace churidars or sit under straight pants and palazzos. Fleece-lined leggings are a lifesaver for outdoor Diwali or walking from the car park.
- **A thin thermal top** with a scoop or V neck stays invisible under most kurtas. Choose a neckline lower than your kurta and three-quarter sleeves if your kurta sleeves are short.
- **Warm socks** in a colour that matches your boots.

Keep these layers thin. Bulky jumpers under a fitted Anarkali spoil the line at the bust and armhole. If you know you will wear thermals every time, mention it when ordering a [custom fit](/custom-stitched-indian-suits-made-to-measure/) piece so we can allow a little extra ease.

## The coat question: length and shape

The coat is the piece everyone sees in photos on the way in, so choose it with your outfit in mind.

| Outfit | Best coat | Why it works |
|---|---|---|
| Floor-length Anarkali | Long wool coat, open or belted loosely | Covers the flare, keeps legs warm |
| Straight kurta set | Knee-length tailored coat or trench | Kurta hem sits just above or below |
| Short kurti with jeans | Pea coat or puffer jacket | Casual and practical |
| Tunic top with trousers | Cropped wool jacket or blazer | Smart for office and dinners |
| Saree or lehenga | Cape or long open cardigan | Leaves the drape intact |

Neutral camel, black, grey and navy coats go with almost every Indian colour. If you own only one, make it a long camel or black wool coat in a slightly A-line cut so it can sit over a flared Anarkali without crushing it.

## Shawls and dupattas that double as warmth

A wool or pashmina-style shawl is the most elegant winter layer in Indian wear. Drape it over both shoulders outdoors, then switch to one shoulder indoors.

You can also wear your dupatta and a shawl together. Pin the light dupatta in place and wrap the shawl over it outside, then remove the shawl at the venue. With a structured outfit like the [Lavender Taffeta Silk Gota Work Anarkali](/products/lavender-taffeta-silk-gota-work-anarkali-suit-set-with-organza-dupatta/), a soft grey or ivory shawl keeps the pastel look calm and pretty.

Choose richer colours for the season. Plum, wine, bottle green and royal blue feel warm and festive against grey skies. The [Plum Purple Embroidered Cotton Suit Set](/products/plum-purple-embroidered-cotton-3-piece-suit/) is a lovely base for a winter dinner with a black coat and burgundy shawl.

## Boots and footwear that suit Indian wear

Juttis are beautiful but they do not love snow or slush. Here are better options:

1. **Ankle boots with a block heel** work with straight pants, palazzos and ankle-length kurtas. Pick suede or leather in black, tan or burgundy.
2. **Knee boots** look smart with shorter kurtas and fitted leggings, almost like a winter tunic dress.
3. **Waterproof boots plus a clutch of juttis.** Wear practical boots to the venue and change inside. Many women keep a small shoe bag for exactly this.

Avoid chunky trainers with a festive Anarkali unless the event is very casual. For an everyday look, a wine or olive tunic over dark jeans and ankle boots is easy and polished. Our [Wine Brown Embroidered Cotton Tunic Top](/products/wine-brown-embroidered-cotton-tunic-top/) layers well under a pea coat.

## Fabric and accessory tips for cold days

- **Cotton is still fine** with thermals underneath and a coat on top. It is breathable indoors, where central heating can feel very warm.
- **Taffeta, georgette and silk** look richer in winter light and hold shape under a coat.
- **Gloves and a beanie** in a neutral tone keep you comfortable on the walk. Take the beanie off before photos to protect your hair.
- **Static control.** Dry heated air causes clingy fabric. A light mist of water or an anti-static spray on the inside of the hem helps.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can I wear a cotton kurta in winter?**
Yes. Add thermal leggings and a thin thermal top under it, and a wool coat outside. Indoors you will be comfortable because most homes and venues are heated.

**What colour coat goes best with Indian outfits?**
Camel, black, grey and navy match almost everything. A long camel coat looks especially elegant over jewel tones.

**How do I keep my Anarkali flare from getting crushed under a coat?**
Choose an A-line or open-front coat and wear it unbelted, or belt it very loosely above the waist.

**Which footwear works for a winter wedding abroad?**
Waterproof ankle boots to travel in, then change into juttis or heels at the venue.
